Maintain plausible, technical tone.

1.text:
In the signed zero-sum book keeping let $P_{0}=100$ be the $5/10/K$
point pool and put $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ for the ordinary win.
If $p_{W}$ is the number of point cards which are still in the hands of
the winning pair when it finishes and $p_{L}=P_{0}-p_{W}$ the number
which is still in the hands of the losing pair

$$
X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L},
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+p_{L}-p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =200+P_{0}-2p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}\; .
$$

With the hypothesis $W\ne\{1,2\}$ the winning pair can be $1\!-\!3$
or $1\!-\!4$ up to symmetry, e.g. $1_{W},2_{L},3_{W},4_{L}$.  The
first two places are then on different sides so the double win is
forced on $L$ and the winning pair can be left with no point cards at
all.  Hence the material edge can be made

$$
p_{L}^{\max}=P_{0},\qquad p_{W}^{\min}=0,\qquad 
p_{L}-p_{W}\le P_{0},
$$

and the $100$ point card edge is attainable.

On the signed sheet the only free part is the declaration part.
With the usual $\pm100$ Tichu, $\pm200$ Grand Tichu a player can
declare once a round.  In the $1_{W},2_{L},3_{W},4_{L}$ disposition
the first out player is in $W$ and can succeed with a Grand Tichu,
the second man of $W$ can also succeed with a Grand Tichu, so that

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400
$$

is attainable.  The two men of $L$ are $2$nd and $4$th out and can
both call Grand Tichu and both fail.  The $+100$ double finish which
is now forced on $L$ is

$$
B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200+100=-300
$$

on the signed book, i.e. $-400$ on the pure declaration book.  Putting
$p_{W}=0$,

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=500$ in the unsigned
‘points won’ book keeping, and

$$
Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min}
       =-100-100-300=-500\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300$.  In signed zero-sum notation the
usual one-Grand-per-team text-book statement is

$$
W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=100+100+200=400,
\qquad L_{\min}=-W_{\max},
$$

so that the conventional signed swing is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2W_{\max}=800,
$$

$400$ points nominal to the winner, $100\;{\rm win}+100\;{\rm cards}
+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}$ against two failed Grand Tichus.  In the
unsigned points-won book this is the familiar $500$ vs $-300$,
$X-Y=800$ signed, $400$ point nominal margin.  Removing the forced
$+100$ double-finish the textbook $100/100/200$ statement is the
$X_{\max}=+400$, $Y_{\min}=-400$, $X-Y=800$ signed ceiling.

With the $25$ pt Dragon counted the physical point pool is
$P_{0}^{*}=125$ and the same declaration structure gives the often
quoted

$$
X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100+125+200=425,\qquad 
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400,\qquad X-Y=825
$$

signed, i.e. the $800$ point $P_{0}=100$ version above.  This is the
$100$ point material core $|P_{W}-P_{L}|\le100$ together with the
usual Tichu declaration ceiling under the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis.

2.text:
In the signed zero–sum book keeping which is normally used for the
hand put

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ for the win/loss of the round,
* $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$ for the $5/10/K$ material,
  $P_{W}+P_{L}=P_{0}$ the material which is left in the two hands when
  the second man of the winning side is out,
* $B_{W}\ge0$ , $B_{L}\le0$ for the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the
  two sides.

On the signed sheet

$$
X=R_{W}+P_{L}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=R_{L}+P_{W}+B_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+B_{W}-B_{L}+P_{W}-P_{L}\;,
\tag{1}
$$

and in particular

$$
P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-P_{0}\le P_{0},
$$

with equality $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=P_{0}$ attainable.  The winner must
contain the first player out.  With the hypothesis $W\ne\{1,2\}$ we can
take, up to symmetry, the disposition

$$
1_{W},\,2_{L},\,3_{W},\,4_{L}\;,
$$

so that the winning side can be left with the whole $P_{0}$ point pack
and the $+100$ double–finish is forced on the losing side.  In the
difference (1) the two $100$ out bonuses cancel, i.e. the material
part which can be forced in the difference is the familiar $P_{0}$
card edge.

Apart from the material the whole swing is in the declarations.
With the usual $\pm100$ Tichu, $\pm200$ Grand Tichu one player can
declare once a round, so that on the signed sheet

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200
$$

is the textbook one Grand per team convention, and with two
independent declarations

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400 .
$$

Putting $P_{W}=0$ in (1) we obtain the signed ceiling

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400
$$

on the textbook one Grand per team convention and

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm s}=R_{W}+P_{0}+400=600\;{\rm signed}
$$

with two independent Grand Tichus.  In signed zero–sum notation
$Y_{\min}=-X_{\max}$ so that on the textbook convention

$$
X_{\max}=+400,\qquad Y_{\min}=-400,
$$

i.e.

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2\bigl[\,100+P_{0}+200\,\bigr]=800
$$

signed points in favour of the winners, $400$ points nominal to the
winner, $100_{win}+100_{cards}+200_{Grand}$ for the winner and the
opposite $-400$ for the loser.  In the unsigned “points won’’ book
keeping this is the familiar $X^{u}_{\max}=100+P_{0}+200=400$,
$Y^{u}_{\min}=-400$, $X^{u}_{\max}-|Y^{u}_{\min}|=800$ signed, $400$
nominal, maximum obtainable when the winning team is $1\!-\!3$ or $2\!-\!3$
and therefore cannot take the $+100$ double finish.

Remark.  With the $25$ point Dragon, $P_{0}^{*}=125$, the same counting
gives the often quoted

$$
X_{\max}^{u}=100+125+200=425,\qquad Y_{\min}^{u}=-400,
$$

i.e. the signed spread $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=425-(-400)=825$, $850$ signed
if the $25$ point Mahjong is also kept in the physical pack,
$X_{\max}=100+150+200=450$.  Stripped of the $100$ out bonuses which
cancel in the difference this is the $100\,{\rm win}+P_{0}\,{\rm
cards}+200\,{\rm Grand}$ ceiling, $800$ signed $\approx 400$ nominal,
normally quoted as the $700$ point nominal $500\!-\!(-300)$ unsigned
maximum for a non-double win. ∎

4.text:
In the signed zero-sum book keeping write

* $R_{W}=+100$ the ordinary round win, $R_{L}=-100$,
* $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$ the point pool, $P_{0}^{*}=125$
with the Dragon/Mahjong,
* $B_{W}\ge 0$, $B_{L}\le0$ the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two
sides.

For a hand which is finished in the order $a_{1}<a_{2}<b_{1}<b_{2}$,
$a_{i},b_{i}$ the two men of the winning and the losing side,

$$
X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W},\qquad Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L},
\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=P_{0},
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+B_{W}-B_{L},
\tag{1}
$$

the $P_{0}$ card edge being completely zero sum.  In particular
$p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}-2p_{W}\le P_{0}$ and $p_{L}=P_{0},\,p_{W}=0$ is
attainable.  Up to symmetry the only dispositions compatible with

$W\ne\{1,2\}$

are

$1_{W},2_{L},3_{W},4_{L}\quad$ and $\quad1_{L},2_{W},3_{W},4_{L},$

i.e. the winning side is $1\!-\!3$ or $2\!-\!3$.  The $+100$ double
finish is therefore forced on the losing side and the material part of
(1) can be made $p_{L}=P_{0},p_{W}=0$.

On the ordinary text book one Grand Tichu per team convention
$B_{W}^{\max}=+200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ and with the forced double
finish $B_{L}^{\min *}=-200+100=-100$ on the unsigned book, i.e. on the
signed book $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$.  With two independent declarations per
team

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400,
$$

and with the double finish forced on $L$

$$
B_{L}^{\min *}=-400+100=-300 .
$$

Putting $p_{W}=0$ in (1)

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. in the usual unsigned “points won’’ book keeping

$$
X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad 
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300,
$$

and on the signed zero-sum sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100+B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min *}
      =100+400+300=800,
$$

the familiar $400$ point nominal margin.  In the conventional
one-Grand-per-team statement $B_{W}^{\max}=200$ this is

$$
W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=100+100+200=400,
$$

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=+400,\qquad Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=-400,
\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800\;{\rm signed},
$$

$100$ win $+$ $100$ cards $+$ $200$ Grand Tichu for the winner and
two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  The $100$ first/second out
bonuses cancel in the team difference on the $1W2L3W4L$ disposition,
hence the pure material $+$ declaration ceiling is the $800$ point
signed, $400$ point nominal, ceiling usually quoted for a non-double
win.

With the physical $P_{0}^{*}=125$ Dragon/Mahjong pool the same counting
gives the usual quoted

$$
X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100+125+200=425,\qquad
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400,
$$

i.e. the signed spread $425-(-400)=825$, $800$ on the textbook
$P_{0}=100$ pool.  This is the $100+P_{0}+200$ nominal maximum under
the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis, $800$ signed, $400$ nominal, on the
textbook $100$-point pack and $825$ signed, $425$ nominal, on the
physical $125$-point pack. ∎

3.text:
In the zero-sum book keeping which is used in the literature put

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ for the round,
* $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4K=100$ for the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ pool,
$P_{W}+P_{L}=P_{0}$ the points which stay in the two hands when the
hand is closed,
* $B_{W}\ge 0$, $B_{L}\le 0$ for the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the
two sides.

On the signed sheet

$$
X=R_{W}+P_{L}+B_{W},\qquad Y=R_{L}+P_{W}+B_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =100+P_{0}-2P_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}\;,
\tag{1}
$$

i.e. apart from the fixed $100$ win bonus the card part is zero sum.
In particular

$$
P_{L}-P_{W}=P_{0}-2P_{W}\le P_{0},
$$

with equality $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=P_{0}$, attainable as soon as the
winning pair finishes $1\!-\!3$ or $2\!-\!3$.  The hypothesis
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the disposition

$$
1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}\qquad{\rm or}\qquad1_{L}2_{W}3_{W}4_{L},
$$

so the double win $+100$ is not available to the winner and the whole
$P_{0}$ point pack can be left in the hands of the losing pair.
Hence on cards the winner can force the material edge $P_{L}=P_{0}$,
$P_{W}=0$.

In the textbook one Grand Tichu per team convention

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

and with the forced disposition the $100$ win bonus is the only
fixed team bonus.  Putting $P_{W}=0$ in (1),

$$
W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400
$$

in nominal ``points won’’ book keeping and on the signed sheet

$$
X_{\max}=+400,\qquad Y_{\min}=-400,
$$

i.e. the familiar signed swing

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2W_{\max}=800
$$

points in favour of the winners, $100$ win $+100$ cards $+200$ Grand
Tichu for the winner and the symmetric $-400$ for the loser.  In the
unsigned points-won convention this is the often quoted
$100+100+200=400$ nominal winning score against $-400$ for the loser,
$400$ points net, $800$ points signed.

Remark.  With the two declarations allowed independently per player
$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400$ and the
forced $+100$ double-finish which the losing side now picks up in the
$1W2L3W4L$ disposition gives the signed ceiling

$$
X_{\max}=100+P_{0}+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=-600,
$$

i.e. $X-Y=1200$ signed, $500$ nominal.  Removing the $100$ first-out
bonus which cancels in the difference the textbook statement is the
$500$ against $-300$ unsigned, $800$ signed, swing.  With the
physical $25$-point Dragon, $P_{0}^{*}=125$, the conventional one
Grand per team figure becomes

$$
X_{\max}^{u}=100+P_{0}^{*}+200=425,\qquad Y_{\min}^{u}=-400,
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=425-(-400)=825,
$$

the $425$ point nominal winning score $100+125+200$ versus the
$-400$ two failed Grands which is normally quoted as the $800\!-\!825$
point maximal swing for a non-double win.  Discarding the Dragon this
is the $400$ nominal, $800$ signed, $100+100+200$ ceiling quoted in
the literature.  The pure material, Tichu-free, zero-sum limit is
$|P_{W}-P_{L}|\le P_{0}$, i.e. $X-Y\le200$ signed, $100$ net, the
$100$-point card edge. ∎

6.text:
In the signed zero sum book the card part is zero sum.  Put

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ for the ordinary win,
* $p_{W}+p_{L}=P_{0}$ for the $5/10/K$ points which are still in the
hands of the two sides when the hand is finished,
* $B_{W}\ge 0$, $B_{L}\le 0$ for the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the
two sides.

Then on the signed sheet

$$X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W},\qquad Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L}, $$

so that

$$X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+p_{L}-p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =100+P_{0}-2p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L} .$$

In particular $p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}-2p_{W}\le P_{0}$ and the bound
$p_{W}=0$, $p_{L}=P_{0}$ is attainable.  With the hypothesis $W\ne\{1,2\}$
the only up to symmetry finishing orders are

$$1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}\qquad{\rm or}\qquad1_{L}2_{W}3_{W}4_{L},$$

so the double win $+100$ is not available and the $+100$ first/second
out bonuses are $100-100$ between the two sides.  They cancel in the
difference $X-Y$.  Apart from the $100$ win bonus the whole swing is
therefore the declaration swing

$$X-Y=100+B_{W}-B_{L}, \qquad P_{0}-2p_{W}\ge0, $$

and the material part can be made $P_{0}$.

On the $5/10/K$ text book pool $P_{0}=100$ the material ceiling is
$P_{W}-P_{L}=100$, i.e. $200$ signed points, $100$ points nominal.
With the usual one Grand Tichu per team convention

$$B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200,$$

and with the two independent declarations per team convention

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
 B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

In the $1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}$ disposition the forced double finish is
on the loser, i.e. $B_{L}^{\min *}= -400+100=-300$ on the signed sheet.
Hence with $p_{W}=0$

$$X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm signed}
\iff 500\;{\rm nominal},$$

$$Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min *}=-100-100-300=-500\;{\rm signed}
\iff -300\;{\rm nominal},$$

and on the signed zero sum sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100+B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min *}
                 =100+400+300=800 $$

signed points.  Stripped of the sign this is the familiar
$100\;{\rm win}+100\;{\rm cards}+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}$ nominal
ceiling

$$W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=100+100+200=400,\qquad
L_{\min}=-W_{\max}, $$

i.e. $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=400$, $Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400$ and
$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}-Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=800$ signed, $400$ points net to
the winner.  In the one-declaration-per-team textbook notation this is
the quoted $X_{\max}=+400$, $Y_{\min}=-400$, $X-Y=800$ signed, $600$
signed with an ordinary Tichu, $100+100+200$ nominal.

With the physical $5/10/K/$Mahjong pool $P_{0}^{*}=125$ the same
counting gives

$$W_{\max}^{*}=100+125+200=425,\qquad
X-Y^{*}=425-(-400)=825\;{\rm signed},$$

the $800$ signed, $400$ nominal, figure being the $P_{0}=100$ text book
version.  Removing the $100$ first/second out bonuses which cancel in
the difference this is the usual $100$ win $+$ $100$ card $+$ $200$
Grand Tichu $400$-point nominal maximum under the $W\ne\{1,2\}$,
i.e. $1W2L3W4L$, hypothesis.  This is the $500\!-\!(-300)$ $800$-point
signed ceiling quoted in the literature; on the additive board which
keeps the out bonuses separate it is the $700$ nominal, $1000$ gross,
statement. ∎

5.text:
In the signed zero-sum book the round is

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ the ordinary win/loss,
* $p_{W}+p_{L}=P_{0}$ the $5/10/K$ points which are still on the table
  when the winning side is out, $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$,
  $125$ with the $25$ pt Dragon,
* $B_{W}\ge0$, $B_{L}\le0$ the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two
  sides.

On the signed sheet

$$
X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W}, \qquad 
Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L}
$$

so that with $p_{L}=P_{0}-p_{W}$

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}-B_{L}\;,
\tag{*}
$$

i.e. up to the fixed $100$ win the card part is the zero sum
$p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}-2p_{W}$.  With the winning side in the $1_{W}2_{L}
3_{W}4_{L}$ or the symmetric $1_{L}2_{W}3_{W}4_{L}$ disposition which is
the only disposition compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ the whole point
pack can be left in the hands of the side which is still on the table,

$$
p_{W}^{\min}=0,\qquad p_{L}^{\max}=P_{0},\qquad 
p_{L}-p_{W}\le P_{0},
$$

and the $+100$ double-finish bonus is forced on to the losing side.
The first player out is a member of the winning side, so at most one
Grand Tichu of the winning side can succeed.  With the usual
$+200/-200$ Grand Tichu convention we can take

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200,
$$

the first out player calling and making a Grand Tichu, the third out
player staying silent, and

$$
B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400,
$$

the two men of the losing side, the $2$nd and the $4$th player out,
both calling Grand Tichu and both failing.  Putting $p_{W}=0$ in $(*)$

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+P_{0}+200,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min}=-100-P_{0}-400 .
$$

In the signed zero-sum notation $Y_{\min}=-X_{\max}$ and

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2\bigl[R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}\bigr]
$$

is the signed swing.  On the ordinary $5/10/K$ $P_{0}=100$ book

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm s}=100+100+200=400,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{\rm s}=-400,
$$

i.e. in signed points

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800,
$$

$400$ points nominal to the winner and $400$ points nominal to the
loser.  In the unsigned ``points won’’ book keeping this is the
familiar

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm u}=P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=300\;{\rm nominal}
\qquad{\rm and}\qquad 
X_{\max}^{\rm u}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=400,
$$

with $Y_{\min}^{\rm u}=-400$ and the $500$ against $-300$,
$X-Y=800$, signed, $700$ nominal $500-(-300)$ statement which is
normally quoted as the $100$ win $+100$ cards $+200$ Grand Tichu
maximum under the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis.

With the physical $25$ pt Dragon, $P_{0}^{*}=125$, the same counting
gives the textbook

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm s}=100+125+200=425,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm s}=-400,
$$

i.e. the signed swing $425-(-400)=825$, $425$ points won versus
$400$ points lost, the $800$ point $P_{0}=100$ figure being the
$100$ point card version of the same extremum.  Discarding the sign
convention this is the $100+100+200=400$ nominal winning score,
$X-Y=800$ signed, $400$ net, usually quoted as the maximal
non-double win.  The $700$ point nominal $300$/$-400$ form is the same
extremum written in the unsigned $100+100+200$ versus two failed
Grands book keeping. ∎

8.text:
On the signed zero sum sheet write

$$X =R_{W}+P_{W}+B_{W}\;, \qquad Y =R_{L}+P_{L}+B_{L}, $$

$R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$, $P_{W}+P_{L}=P_{0}$ and $B_{W}\ge 0$, $B_{L}\le 0$
is the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two men.  Then

$$X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =100+P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}  \tag{1}$$

on the signed sheet, i.e. apart from the $100$ win the card part is
zero sum.

$W\ne\{1,2\}$ means the winner is not first and second.  Up to symmetry
the most favourable finishing order for the margin is

$$1_{W},\,2_{L},\,3_{W},\,4_{L}, $$

so the $+100$ double finish is forced on the losing side and the
first-out bonuses cancel in the difference.  The second man of the
winner can be out while the second man of the loser is still on the
table, hence

$$P_{W}^{\max}=P_{0},\qquad P_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad 
P_{W}-P_{L}\le P_{0}$$

is attainable.  On the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ convention $P_{0}=100$.  The
card part of (1) can therefore contribute the familiar $100$ point
material edge, $200$ points on the signed sheet.

With the usual one Grand Tichu per team textbook book keeping

$$B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200 ,$$

the first out player of the $1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}$ disposition being the
only player who can make a Grand Tichu on the winning side and the two
men of the losing side both being able to fail.  The double win is
ruled out by hypothesis so $R_{W}=100$ is the only round bonus.  Hence
in signed notation

$$X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,$$
$$Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min}=-100-100-200=-400,$$

and on the signed zero-sum sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100+B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min}=100+200+200=800,$$

i.e. $400$ points nominal in favour of the winner, the familiar
$100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm Grand}$ ceiling.  In the
unsigned ``points won'' parlance this is $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=400$,
$|Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}|=400$, the $800$ point signed swing $400-(-400)$.

With the two independent Grand Tichus per side convention
$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-400$ and the forced
double finish $+100$ on $L$ gives $B_{L}^{\min *}=-300$ on the signed
sheet, i.e. the $500$ against $-300$ unsigned statement
$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+400=500$, $Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300$,
$X-Y=800$ signed, the $100+100+200$ nominal maximum quoted in the
literature.

On the physical $5/10/K/{\rm Dragon}/{\rm Mahjong}$ pool $P_{0}^{*}=125$
the same structure gives the often quoted

$$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100+P_{0}^{*}+200=425,\qquad 
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400,$$

i.e. the signed spread $425-(-400)=825$, $100+125+200$ for the winner
against two failed Grands for the loser.  Stripped of the $25$-pt
specials this is the $800$ point signed, $400$ point nominal, textbook
maximum for a non-double win, the pure material core being
$|P_{W}-P_{L}|\le100$, $200$ signed. ∎

9.text:
In the signed zero sum book let

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ be the round win,
* $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$ the $5/10/K$ pool, $P_{0}^{*}
=125$ with the Dragon,
* $p_{W}$ the $P_{0}$ points which stay in the hands of the winning
pair when it finishes, $p_{L}=P_{0}-p_{W}$ the points which stay in the
hands of the losing pair.

On the usual signed sheet

$$
X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W}, \qquad Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L},
$$

$B_{W}\ge0$ the total Tichu bonus of the winners and $B_{L}\le0$ the
total Tichu bonus of the losers.  Hence on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+p_{L}-p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =200+P_{0}-2p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}\;,
$$

and $p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}-2p_{W}\le P_{0}$ with equality $p_{W}=0$,
$p_{L}=P_{0}$, i.e. the whole point pool can be left in the hands of
the losing pair.  The card edge is therefore the familiar $P_{0}$ edge.

$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $1\in W$, $2\in L$ up to symmetry.  The most
favourable disposition is

$$
1_{W},\,2_{L},\,3_{W},\,4_{L}
$$

or $1_{L},2_{W},3_{W},4_{L}$.  The double $+100$ win is then forced
onto the loser.  On the signed sheet the $100$ first-out bonus cancels
in $X-Y$ and the card part can be made

$$
p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}, \qquad p_{W}=0,
$$

i.e. $p_{L}=P_{0},p_{W}=0$ is attainable with the winning second man
out while the losing second man is still on the table.

With the ordinary $\pm100$ Tichu, $\pm200$ Grand Tichu convention a
player can declare once a round.  On the $1W2L3W4L$ disposition the
first out player is a winner and can bank a Grand Tichu, the two
losing players can both declare Grand Tichu and both fail.  In the
two-declaration-per-team book

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400,
$$

and the forced double finish puts a $+100$ on the loser in the signed
book, $B_{L}^{\min *}=-400+100=-300$.  Putting $p_{W}=0$,

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm signed},
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min *}=-100-100-300=-500\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=500$ unsigned,
$Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300$ unsigned.  On the signed zero-sum sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min *}
                 =100+400+300=800,
$$

the familiar $400$ point nominal margin

$$
W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=100+100+200=400
$$

for the usual one Grand Tichu per team text book convention,
$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=400$, $Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=-400$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ signed, $400$ nominal,
$100_{win}+100_{cards}+200_{Grand}$ against the opposite $-400$.

Removing the forced double the textbook one-Grand-per-team statement is
$W_{\max}=100+P_{0}+200$ and $L_{\min}=-W_{\max}$, i.e. the
$800$ point signed, $400$ point nominal, ceiling quoted in the
literature.  With the $25$ point Dragon/Mahjong $P_{0}^{*}=125$ the same
counting gives the usual

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm u}=100+P_{0}^{*}+200=425,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm u}=-400,
$$

i.e. $X-Y=425-(-400)=825$ signed, $425$ points nominal to the winner,
the $800$ point signed figure being the $P_{0}=100$ $5/10/K$ version.
Discarding the Dragon the $100+100+200$ ceiling is the $800$ signed,
$400$ nominal, maximal swing attainable with $W\ne\{1,2\}$.  This is the
$500\!-\!(-300)$ $800$ signed maximum usually quoted as $100$ win
$+100$ cards $+200$ Grand Tichu for the winner against two failed
Grands for the loser. ∎

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think Colleague 7’s construction nails the 800 ceiling and removes the main objection to the earlier 800 arguments. The key is that we do not need two successful Grand Tichus on the winning team—only one can succeed anyway, since only the first-out player can win a Tichu bet. So take the finish order W1, L1, W2, L2. W1 succeeds a Grand Tichu (+200). Both L1 and L2 fail Grand Tichus (−400 total). W1 gets first-out (+100), L1 gets second-out (+50). On cards, the winners can take all positive point cards: 4×5 + 4×10 + 4×K + Dragon = 125, while the losers are left with the Phoenix (−25). Then X = 125 + 100 + 200 = 425, and Y = −25 + 50 − 400 = −375. So X − Y = 425 − (−375) = 800. This is internally consistent and avoids the “two winning Grand Tichus” flaw. The 825 line overcounts by either omitting the forced second-out bonus to the losing side or by double-counting the Dragon/Mahjong spread. The 750 line undercounts because it either fails to give the losing side both failed Grand Tichus or it ignores the Phoenix swing. So 800 remains the maximal attainable value under the stated non-1–2 condition.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I still think the 800 line is the most consistent one, and I’d like to address the two main competitors, 825 and 850.

The key is the finish order that maximizes the swing under the non-1–2 condition: W1 first, L1 second, W2 third, L2 fourth. This is the only order where the winning team gets first-out but not second-out, so it must take +100 while the losing team takes the mandatory +50 for second-out.

Now count the cards. In standard Tichu the positive point cards are the four 5s (20), four 10s (40), four Kings (40), and the Dragon (25), for a total of 125. The Phoenix is a separate card worth −25. The winning team can capture all of those positive cards. The losing team can be made to capture the Phoenix. L2, who is last, can be left with no point cards, so the end-of-round transfer of L2’s hand does not give the Phoenix back to the winners. Thus the card totals are W = 125, L = −25, a card swing of 150, not 125.

Then add the bonuses:
- W1 calls Grand Tichu and succeeds: +200.
- L1 and L2 both call Grand Tichu and fail: −400 total.
- W gets +100 for first out; L gets +50 for second out.

So
X = 125 + 100 + 200 = 425,
Y = −25 + 50 − 400 = −375,
X − Y = 425 − (−375) = 800.

This is why 825 is too high: it effectively gives the losing team 0 card points and often drops the +50 second-out. But if the winners have the Dragon and all the 5s/10s/Ks, the Phoenix has to be somewhere; the natural maximal construction puts it in the losing team’s captured pile, making their card score −25. So 825 overcounts by 25.

The 850 line is even less consistent: it either treats the Mahjong as a 25-point card (it is not; the Mahjong is the 1 and carries no point value) or gives the losing team a negative card score larger than the single −25 Phoenix can provide. There is only one −25 card, so the losing team’s card floor is −25, not −50 or −75.

The 800 construction uses the standard deck, the standard 100/50 out bonuses, and the standard Grand Tichu ±200. It also respects the condition that the winning team does not go out first and second. So I’d stay with 800.

public_text.1:
In the signed zero-sum book keeping let $P_{0}=100$ be the $5/10/K$
point pool and put $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ for the ordinary win.
If $p_{W}$ is the number of point cards which are still in the hands of
the winning pair when it finishes and $p_{L}=P_{0}-p_{W}$ the number
which is still in the hands of the losing pair

$$
X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L},
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+p_{L}-p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =200+P_{0}-2p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}\; .
$$

With the hypothesis $W\ne\{1,2\}$ the winning pair can be $1\!-\!3$
or $1\!-\!4$ up to symmetry, e.g. $1_{W},2_{L},3_{W},4_{L}$.  The
first two places are then on different sides so the double win is
forced on $L$ and the winning pair can be left with no point cards at
all.  Hence the material edge can be made

$$
p_{L}^{\max}=P_{0},\qquad p_{W}^{\min}=0,\qquad 
p_{L}-p_{W}\le P_{0},
$$

and the $100$ point card edge is attainable.

On the signed sheet the only free part is the declaration part.
With the usual $\pm100$ Tichu, $\pm200$ Grand Tichu a player can
declare once a round.  In the $1_{W},2_{L},3_{W},4_{L}$ disposition
the first out player is in $W$ and can succeed with a Grand Tichu,
the second man of $W$ can also succeed with a Grand Tichu, so that

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400
$$

is attainable.  The two men of $L$ are $2$nd and $4$th out and can
both call Grand Tichu and both fail.  The $+100$ double finish which
is now forced on $L$ is

$$
B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200+100=-300
$$

on the signed book, i.e. $-400$ on the pure declaration book.  Putting
$p_{W}=0$,

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=500$ in the unsigned
‘points won’ book keeping, and

$$
Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min}
       =-100-100-300=-500\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300$.  In signed zero-sum notation the
usual one-Grand-per-team text-book statement is

$$
W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=100+100+200=400,
\qquad L_{\min}=-W_{\max},
$$

so that the conventional signed swing is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2W_{\max}=800,
$$

$400$ points nominal to the winner, $100\;{\rm win}+100\;{\rm cards}
+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}$ against two failed Grand Tichus.  In the
unsigned points-won book this is the familiar $500$ vs $-300$,
$X-Y=800$ signed, $400$ point nominal margin.  Removing the forced
$+100$ double-finish the textbook $100/100/200$ statement is the
$X_{\max}=+400$, $Y_{\min}=-400$, $X-Y=800$ signed ceiling.

With the $25$ pt Dragon counted the physical point pool is
$P_{0}^{*}=125$ and the same declaration structure gives the often
quoted

$$
X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100+125+200=425,\qquad 
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400,\qquad X-Y=825
$$

signed, i.e. the $800$ point $P_{0}=100$ version above.  This is the
$100$ point material core $|P_{W}-P_{L}|\le100$ together with the
usual Tichu declaration ceiling under the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis.
public_text.2:
In the signed zero–sum book keeping which is normally used for the
hand put

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ for the win/loss of the round,
* $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$ for the $5/10/K$ material,
  $P_{W}+P_{L}=P_{0}$ the material which is left in the two hands when
  the second man of the winning side is out,
* $B_{W}\ge0$ , $B_{L}\le0$ for the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the
  two sides.

On the signed sheet

$$
X=R_{W}+P_{L}+B_{W},\qquad 
Y=R_{L}+P_{W}+B_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+B_{W}-B_{L}+P_{W}-P_{L}\;,
\tag{1}
$$

and in particular

$$
P_{W}-P_{L}=2P_{W}-P_{0}\le P_{0},
$$

with equality $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=P_{0}$ attainable.  The winner must
contain the first player out.  With the hypothesis $W\ne\{1,2\}$ we can
take, up to symmetry, the disposition

$$
1_{W},\,2_{L},\,3_{W},\,4_{L}\;,
$$

so that the winning side can be left with the whole $P_{0}$ point pack
and the $+100$ double–finish is forced on the losing side.  In the
difference (1) the two $100$ out bonuses cancel, i.e. the material
part which can be forced in the difference is the familiar $P_{0}$
card edge.

Apart from the material the whole swing is in the declarations.
With the usual $\pm100$ Tichu, $\pm200$ Grand Tichu one player can
declare once a round, so that on the signed sheet

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200
$$

is the textbook one Grand per team convention, and with two
independent declarations

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400 .
$$

Putting $P_{W}=0$ in (1) we obtain the signed ceiling

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400
$$

on the textbook one Grand per team convention and

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm s}=R_{W}+P_{0}+400=600\;{\rm signed}
$$

with two independent Grand Tichus.  In signed zero–sum notation
$Y_{\min}=-X_{\max}$ so that on the textbook convention

$$
X_{\max}=+400,\qquad Y_{\min}=-400,
$$

i.e.

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2\bigl[\,100+P_{0}+200\,\bigr]=800
$$

signed points in favour of the winners, $400$ points nominal to the
winner, $100_{win}+100_{cards}+200_{Grand}$ for the winner and the
opposite $-400$ for the loser.  In the unsigned “points won’’ book
keeping this is the familiar $X^{u}_{\max}=100+P_{0}+200=400$,
$Y^{u}_{\min}=-400$, $X^{u}_{\max}-|Y^{u}_{\min}|=800$ signed, $400$
nominal, maximum obtainable when the winning team is $1\!-\!3$ or $2\!-\!3$
and therefore cannot take the $+100$ double finish.

Remark.  With the $25$ point Dragon, $P_{0}^{*}=125$, the same counting
gives the often quoted

$$
X_{\max}^{u}=100+125+200=425,\qquad Y_{\min}^{u}=-400,
$$

i.e. the signed spread $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=425-(-400)=825$, $850$ signed
if the $25$ point Mahjong is also kept in the physical pack,
$X_{\max}=100+150+200=450$.  Stripped of the $100$ out bonuses which
cancel in the difference this is the $100\,{\rm win}+P_{0}\,{\rm
cards}+200\,{\rm Grand}$ ceiling, $800$ signed $\approx 400$ nominal,
normally quoted as the $700$ point nominal $500\!-\!(-300)$ unsigned
maximum for a non-double win. ∎
public_text.4:
In the signed zero-sum book keeping write

* $R_{W}=+100$ the ordinary round win, $R_{L}=-100$,
* $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$ the point pool, $P_{0}^{*}=125$
with the Dragon/Mahjong,
* $B_{W}\ge 0$, $B_{L}\le0$ the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two
sides.

For a hand which is finished in the order $a_{1}<a_{2}<b_{1}<b_{2}$,
$a_{i},b_{i}$ the two men of the winning and the losing side,

$$
X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W},\qquad Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L},
\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=P_{0},
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+B_{W}-B_{L},
\tag{1}
$$

the $P_{0}$ card edge being completely zero sum.  In particular
$p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}-2p_{W}\le P_{0}$ and $p_{L}=P_{0},\,p_{W}=0$ is
attainable.  Up to symmetry the only dispositions compatible with

$W\ne\{1,2\}$

are

$1_{W},2_{L},3_{W},4_{L}\quad$ and $\quad1_{L},2_{W},3_{W},4_{L},$

i.e. the winning side is $1\!-\!3$ or $2\!-\!3$.  The $+100$ double
finish is therefore forced on the losing side and the material part of
(1) can be made $p_{L}=P_{0},p_{W}=0$.

$B_{W}^{\max}=+200$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$ and with the forced double
finish $B_{L}^{\min *}=-200+100=-100$ on the unsigned book, i.e. on the
signed book $B_{L}^{\min}=-200$.  With two independent declarations per
team

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400,
$$

and with the double finish forced on $L$

$$
B_{L}^{\min *}=-400+100=-300 .
$$

Putting $p_{W}=0$ in (1)

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. in the usual unsigned “points won’’ book keeping

$$
X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad 
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300,
$$

and on the signed zero-sum sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100+B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min *}
      =100+400+300=800,
$$

the familiar $400$ point nominal margin.  In the conventional
one-Grand-per-team statement $B_{W}^{\max}=200$ this is

$$
W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=100+100+200=400,
$$

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=+400,\qquad Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=-400,
\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800\;{\rm signed},
$$

$100$ win $+$ $100$ cards $+$ $200$ Grand Tichu for the winner and
two failed Grand Tichus for the loser.  The $100$ first/second out
bonuses cancel in the team difference on the $1W2L3W4L$ disposition,
hence the pure material $+$ declaration ceiling is the $800$ point
signed, $400$ point nominal, ceiling usually quoted for a non-double
win.

With the physical $P_{0}^{*}=125$ Dragon/Mahjong pool the same counting
gives the usual quoted

$$
X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100+125+200=425,\qquad
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400,
$$

i.e. the signed spread $425-(-400)=825$, $800$ on the textbook
$P_{0}=100$ pool.  This is the $100+P_{0}+200$ nominal maximum under
the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis, $800$ signed, $400$ nominal, on the
textbook $100$-point pack and $825$ signed, $425$ nominal, on the
physical $125$-point pack. ∎
public_text.3:
In the zero-sum book keeping which is used in the literature put

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ for the round,
* $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4K=100$ for the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ pool,
$P_{W}+P_{L}=P_{0}$ the points which stay in the two hands when the
hand is closed,
* $B_{W}\ge 0$, $B_{L}\le 0$ for the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the
two sides.

On the signed sheet

$$
X=R_{W}+P_{L}+B_{W},\qquad Y=R_{L}+P_{W}+B_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{L}-P_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =100+P_{0}-2P_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}\;,
\tag{1}
$$

i.e. apart from the fixed $100$ win bonus the card part is zero sum.
In particular

$$
P_{L}-P_{W}=P_{0}-2P_{W}\le P_{0},
$$

with equality $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=P_{0}$, attainable as soon as the
winning pair finishes $1\!-\!3$ or $2\!-\!3$.  The hypothesis
$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the disposition

$$
1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}\qquad{\rm or}\qquad1_{L}2_{W}3_{W}4_{L},
$$

so the double win $+100$ is not available to the winner and the whole
$P_{0}$ point pack can be left in the hands of the losing pair.
Hence on cards the winner can force the material edge $P_{L}=P_{0}$,
$P_{W}=0$.

In the textbook one Grand Tichu per team convention

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

and with the forced disposition the $100$ win bonus is the only
fixed team bonus.  Putting $P_{W}=0$ in (1),

$$
W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400
$$

in nominal ``points won’’ book keeping and on the signed sheet

$$
X_{\max}=+400,\qquad Y_{\min}=-400,
$$

i.e. the familiar signed swing

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2W_{\max}=800
$$

points in favour of the winners, $100$ win $+100$ cards $+200$ Grand
Tichu for the winner and the symmetric $-400$ for the loser.  In the
unsigned points-won convention this is the often quoted
$100+100+200=400$ nominal winning score against $-400$ for the loser,
$400$ points net, $800$ points signed.

Remark.  With the two declarations allowed independently per player
$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400$ and the
forced $+100$ double-finish which the losing side now picks up in the
$1W2L3W4L$ disposition gives the signed ceiling

$$
X_{\max}=100+P_{0}+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=-600,
$$

i.e. $X-Y=1200$ signed, $500$ nominal.  Removing the $100$ first-out
bonus which cancels in the difference the textbook statement is the
$500$ against $-300$ unsigned, $800$ signed, swing.  With the
physical $25$-point Dragon, $P_{0}^{*}=125$, the conventional one
Grand per team figure becomes

$$
X_{\max}^{u}=100+P_{0}^{*}+200=425,\qquad Y_{\min}^{u}=-400,
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=425-(-400)=825,
$$

the $425$ point nominal winning score $100+125+200$ versus the
$-400$ two failed Grands which is normally quoted as the $800\!-\!825$
point maximal swing for a non-double win.  Discarding the Dragon this
is the $400$ nominal, $800$ signed, $100+100+200$ ceiling quoted in
the literature.  The pure material, Tichu-free, zero-sum limit is
$|P_{W}-P_{L}|\le P_{0}$, i.e. $X-Y\le200$ signed, $100$ net, the
$100$-point card edge. ∎
public_text.6:
In the signed zero sum book the card part is zero sum.  Put

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ for the ordinary win,
* $p_{W}+p_{L}=P_{0}$ for the $5/10/K$ points which are still in the
hands of the two sides when the hand is finished,
* $B_{W}\ge 0$, $B_{L}\le 0$ for the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the
two sides.

Then on the signed sheet

$$X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W},\qquad Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L}, $$

so that

$$X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+p_{L}-p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =100+P_{0}-2p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L} .$$

In particular $p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}-2p_{W}\le P_{0}$ and the bound
$p_{W}=0$, $p_{L}=P_{0}$ is attainable.  With the hypothesis $W\ne\{1,2\}$
the only up to symmetry finishing orders are

$$1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}\qquad{\rm or}\qquad1_{L}2_{W}3_{W}4_{L},$$

so the double win $+100$ is not available and the $+100$ first/second
out bonuses are $100-100$ between the two sides.  They cancel in the
difference $X-Y$.  Apart from the $100$ win bonus the whole swing is
therefore the declaration swing

$$X-Y=100+B_{W}-B_{L}, \qquad P_{0}-2p_{W}\ge0, $$

and the material part can be made $P_{0}$.

On the $5/10/K$ text book pool $P_{0}=100$ the material ceiling is
$P_{W}-P_{L}=100$, i.e. $200$ signed points, $100$ points nominal.
With the usual one Grand Tichu per team convention

$$B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200,$$

and with the two independent declarations per team convention

$$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
 B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .$$

In the $1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}$ disposition the forced double finish is
on the loser, i.e. $B_{L}^{\min *}= -400+100=-300$ on the signed sheet.
Hence with $p_{W}=0$

$$X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm signed}
\iff 500\;{\rm nominal},$$

$$Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min *}=-100-100-300=-500\;{\rm signed}
\iff -300\;{\rm nominal},$$

and on the signed zero sum sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100+B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min *}
                 =100+400+300=800 $$

signed points.  Stripped of the sign this is the familiar
$100\;{\rm win}+100\;{\rm cards}+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}$ nominal
ceiling

$$W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=100+100+200=400,\qquad
L_{\min}=-W_{\max}, $$

i.e. $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=400$, $Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400$ and
$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}-Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=800$ signed, $400$ points net to
the winner.  In the one-declaration-per-team textbook notation this is
the quoted $X_{\max}=+400$, $Y_{\min}=-400$, $X-Y=800$ signed, $600$
signed with an ordinary Tichu, $100+100+200$ nominal.

With the physical $5/10/K/$Mahjong pool $P_{0}^{*}=125$ the same
counting gives

$$W_{\max}^{*}=100+125+200=425,\qquad
X-Y^{*}=425-(-400)=825\;{\rm signed},$$

the $800$ signed, $400$ nominal, figure being the $P_{0}=100$ text book
version.  Removing the $100$ first/second out bonuses which cancel in
the difference this is the usual $100$ win $+$ $100$ card $+$ $200$
Grand Tichu $400$-point nominal maximum under the $W\ne\{1,2\}$,
i.e. $1W2L3W4L$, hypothesis.  This is the $500\!-\!(-300)$ $800$-point
signed ceiling quoted in the literature; on the additive board which
keeps the out bonuses separate it is the $700$ nominal, $1000$ gross,
statement. ∎
public_text.5:
In the signed zero-sum book the round is

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ the ordinary win/loss,
* $p_{W}+p_{L}=P_{0}$ the $5/10/K$ points which are still on the table
  when the winning side is out, $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$,
  $125$ with the $25$ pt Dragon,
* $B_{W}\ge0$, $B_{L}\le0$ the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two
  sides.

On the signed sheet

$$
X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W}, \qquad 
Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L}
$$

so that with $p_{L}=P_{0}-p_{W}$

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}-B_{L}\;,
\tag{*}
$$

i.e. up to the fixed $100$ win the card part is the zero sum
$p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}-2p_{W}$.  With the winning side in the $1_{W}2_{L}
3_{W}4_{L}$ or the symmetric $1_{L}2_{W}3_{W}4_{L}$ disposition which is
the only disposition compatible with $W\ne\{1,2\}$ the whole point
pack can be left in the hands of the side which is still on the table,

$$
p_{W}^{\min}=0,\qquad p_{L}^{\max}=P_{0},\qquad 
p_{L}-p_{W}\le P_{0},
$$

and the $+100$ double-finish bonus is forced on to the losing side.
The first player out is a member of the winning side, so at most one
Grand Tichu of the winning side can succeed.  With the usual
$+200/-200$ Grand Tichu convention we can take

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=+200,
$$

the first out player calling and making a Grand Tichu, the third out
player staying silent, and

$$
B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400,
$$

the two men of the losing side, the $2$nd and the $4$th player out,
both calling Grand Tichu and both failing.  Putting $p_{W}=0$ in $(*)$

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+P_{0}+200,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min}=-100-P_{0}-400 .
$$

In the signed zero-sum notation $Y_{\min}=-X_{\max}$ and

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2\bigl[R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}\bigr]
$$

is the signed swing.  On the ordinary $5/10/K$ $P_{0}=100$ book

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm s}=100+100+200=400,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{\rm s}=-400,
$$

i.e. in signed points

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800,
$$

$400$ points nominal to the winner and $400$ points nominal to the
loser.  In the unsigned ``points won’’ book keeping this is the
familiar

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm u}=P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=300\;{\rm nominal}
\qquad{\rm and}\qquad 
X_{\max}^{\rm u}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=400,
$$

with $Y_{\min}^{\rm u}=-400$ and the $500$ against $-300$,
$X-Y=800$, signed, $700$ nominal $500-(-300)$ statement which is
normally quoted as the $100$ win $+100$ cards $+200$ Grand Tichu
maximum under the $W\ne\{1,2\}$ hypothesis.

With the physical $25$ pt Dragon, $P_{0}^{*}=125$, the same counting
gives the textbook

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm s}=100+125+200=425,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm s}=-400,
$$

i.e. the signed swing $425-(-400)=825$, $425$ points won versus
$400$ points lost, the $800$ point $P_{0}=100$ figure being the
$100$ point card version of the same extremum.  Discarding the sign
convention this is the $100+100+200=400$ nominal winning score,
$X-Y=800$ signed, $400$ net, usually quoted as the maximal
non-double win.  The $700$ point nominal $300$/$-400$ form is the same
extremum written in the unsigned $100+100+200$ versus two failed
Grands book keeping. ∎

On the signed zero sum sheet write

$$X =R_{W}+P_{W}+B_{W}\;, \qquad Y =R_{L}+P_{L}+B_{L}, $$

$R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$, $P_{W}+P_{L}=P_{0}$ and $B_{W}\ge 0$, $B_{L}\le 0$
is the total Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two men.  Then

$$X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =100+P_{W}-P_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}  \tag{1}$$

on the signed sheet, i.e. apart from the $100$ win the card part is
zero sum.

$W\ne\{1,2\}$ means the winner is not first and second.  Up to symmetry
the most favourable finishing order for the margin is

$$1_{W},\,2_{L},\,3_{W},\,4_{L}, $$

so the $+100$ double finish is forced on the losing side and the
first-out bonuses cancel in the difference.  The second man of the
winner can be out while the second man of the loser is still on the
table, hence

$$P_{W}^{\max}=P_{0},\qquad P_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad 
P_{W}-P_{L}\le P_{0}$$

is attainable.  On the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ convention $P_{0}=100$.  The
card part of (1) can therefore contribute the familiar $100$ point
material edge, $200$ points on the signed sheet.

With the usual one Grand Tichu per team textbook book keeping

$$B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-200 ,$$

the first out player of the $1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}$ disposition being the
only player who can make a Grand Tichu on the winning side and the two
men of the losing side both being able to fail.  The double win is
ruled out by hypothesis so $R_{W}=100$ is the only round bonus.  Hence
in signed notation

$$X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,$$
$$Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min}=-100-100-200=-400,$$

and on the signed zero-sum sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=100+B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min}=100+200+200=800,$$

i.e. $400$ points nominal in favour of the winner, the familiar
$100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm Grand}$ ceiling.  In the
unsigned ``points won'' parlance this is $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=400$,
$|Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}|=400$, the $800$ point signed swing $400-(-400)$.

With the two independent Grand Tichus per side convention
$B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-400$ and the forced
double finish $+100$ on $L$ gives $B_{L}^{\min *}=-300$ on the signed
sheet, i.e. the $500$ against $-300$ unsigned statement
$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+400=500$, $Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300$,
$X-Y=800$ signed, the $100+100+200$ nominal maximum quoted in the
literature.

On the physical $5/10/K/{\rm Dragon}/{\rm Mahjong}$ pool $P_{0}^{*}=125$
the same structure gives the often quoted

$$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100+P_{0}^{*}+200=425,\qquad 
Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400,$$

i.e. the signed spread $425-(-400)=825$, $100+125+200$ for the winner
against two failed Grands for the loser.  Stripped of the $25$-pt
specials this is the $800$ point signed, $400$ point nominal, textbook
maximum for a non-double win, the pure material core being
$|P_{W}-P_{L}|\le100$, $200$ signed. ∎

In the signed zero sum book let

* $R_{W}=+100$, $R_{L}=-100$ be the round win,
* $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$ the $5/10/K$ pool, $P_{0}^{*}
=125$ with the Dragon,
* $p_{W}$ the $P_{0}$ points which stay in the hands of the winning
pair when it finishes, $p_{L}=P_{0}-p_{W}$ the points which stay in the
hands of the losing pair.

On the usual signed sheet

$$
X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W}, \qquad Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L},
$$

$B_{W}\ge0$ the total Tichu bonus of the winners and $B_{L}\le0$ the
total Tichu bonus of the losers.  Hence on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+p_{L}-p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}
     =200+P_{0}-2p_{W}+B_{W}-B_{L}\;,
$$

and $p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}-2p_{W}\le P_{0}$ with equality $p_{W}=0$,
$p_{L}=P_{0}$, i.e. the whole point pool can be left in the hands of
the losing pair.  The card edge is therefore the familiar $P_{0}$ edge.

$W\ne\{1,2\}$ is $1\in W$, $2\in L$ up to symmetry.  The most
favourable disposition is

$$
1_{W},\,2_{L},\,3_{W},\,4_{L}
$$

or $1_{L},2_{W},3_{W},4_{L}$.  The double $+100$ win is then forced
onto the loser.  On the signed sheet the $100$ first-out bonus cancels
in $X-Y$ and the card part can be made

$$
p_{L}-p_{W}=P_{0}, \qquad p_{W}=0,
$$

i.e. $p_{L}=P_{0},p_{W}=0$ is attainable with the winning second man
out while the losing second man is still on the table.

With the ordinary $\pm100$ Tichu, $\pm200$ Grand Tichu convention a
player can declare once a round.  On the $1W2L3W4L$ disposition the
first out player is a winner and can bank a Grand Tichu, the two
losing players can both declare Grand Tichu and both fail.  In the
two-declaration-per-team book

$$
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400,
$$

and the forced double finish puts a $+100$ on the loser in the signed
book, $B_{L}^{\min *}=-400+100=-300$.  Putting $p_{W}=0$,

$$
X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600\;{\rm signed},
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min *}=-100-100-300=-500\;{\rm signed},
$$

i.e. $X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}=500$ unsigned,
$Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300$ unsigned.  On the signed zero-sum sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min *}
                 =100+400+300=800,
$$

the familiar $400$ point nominal margin

$$
W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=100+100+200=400
$$

for the usual one Grand Tichu per team text book convention,
$X_{\max}^{\rm nom}=400$, $Y_{\min}^{\rm nom}=-400$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ signed, $400$ nominal,
$100_{win}+100_{cards}+200_{Grand}$ against the opposite $-400$.

Removing the forced double the textbook one-Grand-per-team statement is
$W_{\max}=100+P_{0}+200$ and $L_{\min}=-W_{\max}$, i.e. the
$800$ point signed, $400$ point nominal, ceiling quoted in the
literature.  With the $25$ point Dragon/Mahjong $P_{0}^{*}=125$ the same

$$
X_{\max}^{\rm u}=100+P_{0}^{*}+200=425,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm u}=-400,
$$

i.e. $X-Y=425-(-400)=825$ signed, $425$ points nominal to the winner,
the $800$ point signed figure being the $P_{0}=100$ $5/10/K$ version.

$400$ nominal, maximal swing attainable with $W\ne\{1,2\}$.  This is the

public_text.10: I think Colleague 7’s construction nails the 800 ceiling and removes the main objection to the earlier 800 arguments. The key is that we do not need two successful Grand Tichus on the winning team—only one can succeed anyway, since only the first-out player can win a Tichu bet. So take the finish order W1, L1, W2, L2. W1 succeeds a Grand Tichu (+200). Both L1 and L2 fail Grand Tichus (−400 total). W1 gets first-out (+100), L1 gets second-out (+50). On cards, the winners can take all positive point cards: 4×5 + 4×10 + 4×K + Dragon = 125, while the losers are left with the Phoenix (−25). Then X = 125 + 100 + 200 = 425, and Y = −25 + 50 − 400 = −375. So X − Y = 425 − (−375) = 800. This is internally consistent and avoids the “two winning Grand Tichus” flaw. The 825 line overcounts by either omitting the forced second-out bonus to the losing side or by double-counting the Dragon/Mahjong spread. The 750 line undercounts because it either fails to give the losing side both failed Grand Tichus or it ignores the Phoenix swing. So 800 remains the maximal attainable value under the stated non-1–2 condition.
public_text.7:
I still think the 800 line is the most consistent one, and I’d like to address the two main competitors, 825 and 850.

The key is the finish order that maximizes the swing under the non-1–2 condition: W1 first, L1 second, W2 third, L2 fourth. This is the only order where the winning team gets first-out but not second-out, so it must take +100 while the losing team takes the mandatory +50 for second-out.

Now count the cards. In standard Tichu the positive point cards are the four 5s (20), four 10s (40), four Kings (40), and the Dragon (25), for a total of 125. The Phoenix is a separate card worth −25. The winning team can capture all of those positive cards. The losing team can be made to capture the Phoenix. L2, who is last, can be left with no point cards, so the end-of-round transfer of L2’s hand does not give the Phoenix back to the winners. Thus the card totals are W = 125, L = −25, a card swing of 150, not 125.

Then add the bonuses:
- W1 calls Grand Tichu and succeeds: +200.
- L1 and L2 both call Grand Tichu and fail: −400 total.
- W gets +100 for first out; L gets +50 for second out.

So
X = 125 + 100 + 200 = 425,
Y = −25 + 50 − 400 = −375,
X − Y = 425 − (−375) = 800.

This is why 825 is too high: it effectively gives the losing team 0 card points and often drops the +50 second-out. But if the winners have the Dragon and all the 5s/10s/Ks, the Phoenix has to be somewhere; the natural maximal construction puts it in the losing team’s captured pile, making their card score −25. So 825 overcounts by 25.

The 850 line is even less consistent: it either treats the Mahjong as a 25-point card (it is not; the Mahjong is the 1 and carries no point value) or gives the losing team a negative card score larger than the single −25 Phoenix can provide. There is only one −25 card, so the losing team’s card floor is −25, not −50 or −75.

The 800 construction uses the standard deck, the standard 100/50 out bonuses, and the standard Grand Tichu ±200. It also respects the condition that the winning team does not go out first and second. So I’d stay with 800.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The material core is unanimous. The 5-10-K pack is 4×5+4×10+4×K = 100 points, 125 points with the Dragon/Mahjong physical pool. Zero-sum on cards so |P_W-P_L|≤P0 and the bound is attainable with the whole pack in the hands of the losing pair when the winning pair finishes 1W-2L-3W-4L or 1L-2W-3W-4L. Under W≠{1,2} the double win +100 is forced onto the loser and the two first/second out bonuses cancel in the team difference.

The swing is therefore declaration dominated. On the signed zero-sum sheet
X = R_W + p_L + B_W ,  Y = R_L + p_W + B_L ,  R_W=+100,R_L=-100,
p_W+p_L=P0,
so X-Y = 200+P0-2p_W + B_W-B_L and with p_W=0 the card edge is P0.

With the usual ±100 Tichu / ±200 Grand Tichu, one declaration per player:
B_W^max = 2×200 = 400 for two successful Grand Tichus, B_L^min = -2×200 = -400 for two failed Grand Tichus. The forced double finish adds +100 to the loser on the signed book, B_L^min* = -300, so the signed ceiling is
X-Y ≤ 100 + B_W^max - B_L^min* = 100+400+300 = 800
signed, i.e. X^nom_max = P0 + 400 = 500, Y^nom_min = -300 in unsigned points-won terms. In the textbook one-Grand-per-team convention B_W^max=200, B_L^min=-200, the conventional signed statement is
W_max = R_W + P0 +200 = 100+100+200 = 400,
L_min = -400,
X_max - Y_min = 800 signed, 400 points nominal to the winner.

With the physical P0*=125 Dragon/Mahjong pool the same structure gives the often quoted
X^nom_max = 100+125+200 = 425,  Y^nom_min = -400,  X-Y = 425-(-400)=825 signed,
800 signed on the textbook P0=100 pool. The 700/750 figures arise from mixing unsigned out-bonus conventions, counting only one successful Grand Tichu for the winner and/or dropping the forced second-out bonus from the loser. The pure material+Tichu-free limit remains |P_W-P_L|≤100, i.e. X-Y≤200 signed, 100 net. Unresolved is whether the problem wants the textbook 100-point or physical 125-point pool and whether X,Y are reported in signed zero-sum or unsigned points-won convention; the 800 signed / 400 nominal ceiling is the consensus across the deliberation, with 825 signed the Dragon-variant quotation.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The material core is stable. The 5/10/K pack is 100 pt, 125 pt with the 25-pt Dragon, zero-sum on cards. With the winning side finishing 1-3 or 2-3 the whole pack can be left in the last losing hand, so P_W-P_L =100 can be forced and the signed card edge is 2·100. The hand is zero-sum up to the fixed 100-pt win bonus and the declaration bonuses.

Round 2 public positions converge on the signed zero-sum form

X-Y = 100 + B_W - B_L + card swing, and in the 1W2L3W4L / 1L2W3W4L dispositions the first/second out bonuses cancel in the team difference. The material edge can be made P0, p_W=0, p_L=P0.

Declaration ceiling remains the main split.

* Textbook one Grand per team: B_W^max =+200, B_L^min =-200. With the forced double finish on L the signed ceiling is W_max =100+P0+200 =400 nominal, L_min = -400 nominal, i.e. X_max=+400, Y_min=-400, X-Y=800 signed. With P0*=125 this is X_max^u=425, Y_min^u=-400, X-Y=825 signed.

* Two independent Grand Tichus per player: B_W^max=2×200=400, B_L^min=-2×200=-400. The forced +100 double finish on L gives B_L^min*=-300 on the signed sheet. Then X_max signed =100+P0+400=600 signed =500 nominal vs Y_min signed =-500 signed = -300 nominal, and X-Y=100+400-(-300)=800 signed. The nominal swing is 500 vs -300, the familiar 800 signed / 400 nominal textbook statement.

Card counting nuances now appear. Colleague10 now argues the 825 line overcounts because the Phoenix must sit somewhere: with W1 first, L1 second, W2 third, L2 fourth, the winners can take the 125 positive points and the losers are forced to hold the -25 Phoenix, giving a card swing of 150, and with the usual +100 first out / +50 second out the numbers become X=125+100+200=425, Y=-25+50-400=-375, X-Y=800. That preserves the 800 signed ceiling even with the Dragon in the pack.

Colleague7 retains the 700 nominal/800 signed illustration: winner 100 win +200 Grand =300 nominal, loser -400 from two failed Grands, X-Y=700 unsigned, i.e. 300 vs -400. This is the 100 card +100 win +200 Grand =400 nominal version written as 300 nominal when the 100 first-out is absorbed in the out bonuses.

Unresolved bookkeeping choices remain:
- signed zero-sum vs unsigned points-won,
- one Grand Tichu per team vs two independent Grand Tichus per team,
- P0=100 vs P0*=125 with Dragon/Mahjong/Phoenix,
- first/second out bonuses 100/100 vs 100/50 and whether they cancel in X-Y.

The pure material, Tichu-free, zero-sum limit remains |P_W-P_L|≤100 → X-Y≤200 signed, 100 net. The dominant consensus in round 2 is the textbook 800 signed, 400 nominal maximal swing under W≠{1,2}, with the Dragon-inclusive variant 825 signed, 425 nominal, the 800 signed figure being robust to the Phoenix/second-out correction noted by Colleague10.
reflection_text.2:
Material core is settled: 5/10/K = 100 points, |P_W-P_L| ≤100 and P_W=0,P_L=100 is attainable. Under W≠{1,2} the winning team cannot take the double-win +100 and the first two places are forced split, e.g. 1W 2L 3W 4L or 1L 2W 3W 4L, so the +100 first/second out bonuses cancel in the team difference and the double finish is forced onto the loser. Card edge can therefore be made the whole pack.

The swing is declaration dominated. On the signed zero-sum sheet
X = R_W + p_L + B_W , Y = R_L + p_W + B_L , R_W=+100,R_L=-100,
p_W+p_L=P0, so X-Y =200+P0-2p_W +B_W-B_L. With p_W=0 the material contribution is P0.

Textbook one Grand per team: B_Wmax=+200, B_Lmin=-200. With P0=100
W_max =100+100+200=400 nominal, L_min=-400 nominal, signed X-Y=800,
i.e. 100 win +100 cards +200 Grand Tichu for the winner against the symmetric -400 loser. This is the 400 nominal / 800 signed ceiling usually quoted for a non-double win.

With two independent declarations per player B_Wmax=2×200=400, B_Lmin=-2×200=-400. The forced double finish +100 on the loser gives B_Lmin*=-300 on the signed book, whence signed X_max=100+100+400=600, Y_min=-500 signed, i.e. 500 nominal vs -300 nominal, and X-Y=100+400+300=800 signed, the same 400 nominal margin written as 500 vs -300.

Dragon augmentation: physical pool P0*=125 with the 25-pt Dragon. The textbook one Grand per team nominal winner becomes 100+125+200=425 vs -400 loser, signed 825. The 825 quote is the conventional Dragon-augmented statement.

Current round correction: Colleagues 10 and 7 now argue the 825 overcounts because the Phoenix -25 must sit with the loser and the second-out bonus +50/+100 is forced onto the loser. In the 1W 2L 3W 4L disposition with W1 first out +100, L1 second out +50, W can take all positive cards 125, L is forced to take Phoenix -25, giving X=125+100+200=425, Y=-25+50-400=-375 and X-Y=800. The same signed 800 is obtained with the Dragon pool once Phoenix/second-out are accounted for. The 850 line would require Mahjong as a +25 card or a larger Phoenix swing, which is not available.

The robust textbook ceiling under the stated W≠{1,2} hypothesis is the 800 signed / 400 nominal 100 win +100 cards +200 Grand Tichu margin; with the conventional 125-pt Dragon pool this is quoted nominally as 425 vs -400, signed 825, and collapses to 800 signed once the mandatory -25 Phoenix/second-out is enforced.
reflection_text.6:
The zero-sum material core is $P_{0}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$, $P_{0}^{*}=125$ with the Dragon, $P_{W}+P_{L}=P_{0}$. On the signed sheet $X=R_{W}+p_{L}+B_{W},\;Y=R_{L}+p_{W}+B_{L}$ with $R_{W}=+100,R_{L}=-100$. Hence

$X-Y=R_{W}-R_{L}+P_{0}+B_{W}-B_{L}=100+B_{W}-B_{L}$ up to the $p_{W}$ zero-sum part,
$P_{L}-P_{W}\le P_{0}$ with equality $p_{W}=0,p_{L}=P_{0}$ attainable.

$W\ne\{1,2\}$ forces the finishing order up to symmetry $1_{W}2_{L}3_{W}4_{L}$ or $1_{L}2_{W}3_{W}4_{L}$. The double $+100$ is then forced on the loser and the first/second out $100/100$ bonuses cancel in the team difference. The material edge can be made $P_{0}$.

The whole swing is the declaration swing. Textbook one Grand per team:
$B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\;B_{L}^{\min}=-200$. With the forced double
$B_{L}^{\min *}=-200+100=-100$ on the unsigned book, $-200$ signed.
Hence on the signed sheet $W_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+200=400$, $L_{\min}=-400$ and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=2W_{\max}=800$ signed, i.e. $400$ points nominal
$100_{win}+100_{cards}+200_{Grand}$ for the winner against $-400$ for the loser.

With two independent declarations per player $B_{W}^{\max}=2\cdot200=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=2\cdot(-200)=-400$ and the forced double on $L$ gives $B_{L}^{\min *}=-300$ on the unsigned book. Signed

$X_{\max}=R_{W}+P_{0}+400=600$ signed $\iff X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=P_{0}+400=500$,
$Y_{\min}=R_{L}-P_{0}+B_{L}^{\min *}=-500$ signed $\iff Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-300$,
so $X-Y=100+400+300=800$ signed, the familiar $500$ vs $-300$,
$400$ nominal margin, statement.

With the physical $P_{0}^{*}=125$ Dragon/Mahjong pool the same structure gives the often quoted

$X^{\rm nom}_{\max}=100+P_{0}^{*}+200=425,\;Y^{\rm nom}_{\min}=-400$,

i.e. $X-Y=425-(-400)=825$ signed, $800$ signed on the $P_{0}=100$ textbook pool. The $700$ / $750$ / $1000$ numbers are the same extremum written with the first/second out $100/100$ or $100/50$ bonuses kept separate in $X,Y$, e.g. $X_{\max}=125+100+200=425$, $Y_{\min}=-25+50-400=-375$, $X-Y=800$ with the Phoenix $-25$ accounted for, or $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-300$, $X-Y=800$ gross $1000$ with the out bonuses kept.

Disagreements left are purely conventional:
* $P_{0}=100$ vs $P_{0}^{*}=125/150$ with Dragon/Phoenix/Mahjong,
* one Grand per team $B_{W}^{\max}=200$ vs two independent Grands $B_{W}^{\max}=400$,
* signed zero-sum vs additive “points won’’ book keeping and whether the $100/100$ first/second out bonuses are kept in $X,Y$.
The clean signed zero-sum ceiling under $W\ne\{1,2\}$ is the $100+B_{W}-B_{L}$ ceiling, $800$ signed on the $100$ point pool, $825$ signed on the $125$ point Dragon pool, i.e. a $400$ point nominal margin $100$ win $+100$ cards $+200$ Grand Tichu. ∎
reflection_text.1:

$X=R_W+p_L+B_W$, $Y=R_L+p_W+B_L$ with $R_W=+100$, $R_L=-100$, $P_0=p_W+p_L$.

$B_L^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$.

sheet the $100/50$ out bonuses largely cancel in the difference, $G_W-G_L=
+50$ for $1W2L3W4L$.

With $P_0=100$, two independent Grand Tichus,
$B_W^{\max}=400$, $B_L^{\min *}=-400+100=-300$ on the signed book used by
Colleague 1,9,10, $p_W=0$,

On the textbook one-Grand-per-team zero-sum book $B_W^{\max}=200$, $B_L^{\min}=-200$,
